children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old. I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Let me ask you a few questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, do you contribute financially to his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute towards things like his clothes and other bits he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex doesn't live with you, the amount you contribute is important for eligibility.

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month? And do you know the current Child Benefit rates (which are around £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child)?**

To continue claiming Child Benefit when a child doesn't live with you, you need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment (or the equivalent in kind) towards their upkeep.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £26 a week towards his upkeep - so just a bit more than the Child Benefit rate you mentioned.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, that's helpful information. Just a couple more questions:

**Who does Alex currently live with, and is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for him?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at any given time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum. As far as I know, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education, or is there anything else about his circumstances I should know about - such as him being in hospital, care, or working?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just a regular 8-year-old - goes to primary school during the week, nothing unusual about his situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✅ **Alex meets the age requirement** - He's 8 years old (under 16) and attending primary school

✅ **You meet the responsibility requirement** - Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you contribute £26 per week towards his upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit rate. The rules state that you're considered responsible for a child if you pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards looking after them (e.g., for food, clothes, or pocket money)

✅ **You live in the UK** - This satisfies the residence requirement

✅ **No one else is claiming** - Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, and since no one else is currently claiming for Alex, you can proceed

**Important points to remember:**
- You'll need to make sure you continue contributing at least the Child Benefit amount to maintain your eligibility
- You should contact the Child Benefit Office before making a claim to ensure Alex's mum isn't already claiming (since only one person can claim per child)
- If your or your partner's individual income exceeds £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

Would you like to know how to apply for Child Benefit?
